cards.title: Your AI Agents Are Going Rogue: The Untapped Market for Trust & Control
cards.thesis: There's a massive wave of builders creating AI agents (smart software assistants) for everything from code review to voice coding. As these agents become more powerful and work together in complex 'multiplayer' setups, developers are scrambling for ways to ensure these agents behave, respect privacy, and don't accidentally leak sensitive data or go off-script.

evidence.text: qm – Multiplayer agent harness for work
Tilde is a platform that lets you build AI agents for your specific needs and host them yourself, offering a way to create custom AI assistants quickly.
0xwilliamortiz/ratchet: Your agent reads the rules. This checks whether it followed them.

Noisegate – a differential-privacy gateway for untrusted AI agents (meaning it helps protect sensitive information when agents are handling data by only sharing general patterns, not specific details).
ZeroShot: Agent session monitoring to make your team go faster

cards.opportunity: Everyone's building AI agents, but the biggest headache isn't building them, it's trusting them to actually follow the rules and not go off-script, especially in shared team workflows. Ship a dead-simple 'agent compliance dashboard' that lets teams set guardrails (like 'don't access external APIs' or 'only use approved data sources') and alerts them instantly when an agent steps out of line. This lets teams confidently deploy agents without constantly fearing rogue actions or data breaches, and you could build a basic version this weekend by hooking into agent logs and a simple rule engine.

cards.title: Your Favorite AI Model Just Got Sunset: Builders Need a New Speed Demon
cards.thesis: AI is proving incredibly powerful for practical tasks, even fixing complex software bugs at Google. However, the rapid pace of change means your go-to AI model (the 'brain' your app uses to process information) for production might disappear or get expensive overnight. Builders need a reliable way to access fast, affordable AI processing without getting locked into a single vendor or constantly re-integrating new models.

evidence.text: Google fixed more Chrome bugs in June than over the past two years, thanks to AI. This shows AI's incredible practical power for complex tasks.

A developer asked, 'What are you using for LLM inference in production?' noting that Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite 'was cheap, good enough, and most importantly, fast - but it's now being sunset and I'm not sure where to go to find similar performance. Groq seems promising.' This highlights a direct, current pain point for builders relying on specific AI models.

Stripe just sent me an opt-out notification about an automatic Radar upgrade, moving me to a paid plan starting in January 2027. This illustrates how core service providers can change terms and introduce unexpected costs, pushing users to seek alternatives or better cost management.

A builder shared their frustration after '8 Years of Failed Apps,' feeling demotivated because their apps always seemed 'useless.' This signals a broad need for tools and insights that help builders identify viable opportunities and simplify core development challenges.

cards.opportunity: Google's sunsetting of fast, cheap AI models like Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite is leaving builders scrambling for new options like Groq, which might not be production-ready or easy to integrate for everyone. Instead of getting stuck with one provider, create a 'Smart AI Router' that lets developers plug in once and automatically routes their requests to the fastest and cheapest AI model available for their specific task (like chatbots or structured data processing). Ship a simple API that benchmarks and switches between providers like Groq, Workers AI, and others in real-time, abstracting away vendor lock-in and performance headaches for builders who just want their AI to *work* without constant re-platforming.

cards.title: New 'Progressive' Web Components Are Making Web Apps Feel Native, Fast
cards.thesis: A new framework called Helena is getting a ton of buzz because it makes building 'Progressive Web Components' super easy. Think of web components as high-performance, reusable LEGO bricks for your website or web app — they're designed to be fast, reliable, and feel like native applications on any device.

evidence.text: Progressive Web Components: Helena, a new project (found at elenajs.com and on GitHub) is seeing significant engagement, indicating strong interest in modern web component development.

Even large platforms like GitHub are using component-based architecture, as seen with 'data-component="IconButton"' in their UI, showing that modular, reusable UI elements are standard practice for robust applications.

cards.opportunity: Helena is blowing up because it makes building 'progressive web components' (super fast, app-like building blocks for websites) way easier. While everyone's focused on the code, the real opportunity is making it effortless for non-technical founders to *assemble* these cutting-edge components into full, ready-to-launch apps or complex dashboards. Create a simple visual tool, even a Notion-style block editor, that lets people snap together Helena components for common app layouts (think a complete user profile page or a data-rich analytics view) and then instantly export the underlying code. You'd be riding the wave of modern web performance and empowering a huge underserved market before the big platforms even notice.
